title: Marguerite and the Harbor
premise: In 1943, on a storm-battered colonial harbor, Coral Quintana keeps the lighthouse and an unofficial ledger of every family the war has scattered. When the army requisitions the town, her ledger — the only record of the disappeared — is seized as evidence to be rewritten by the victors' historians. Coral smuggles the true names out with the help of a disgraced army cartographer, Elias Voss, and the orphaned girl, Marguerite, she has quietly taken in. As the requisition deadline closes in, Coral must choose between surrendering the truth for amnesty or burning it to keep her found family safe; in the end she trades her keeper's post for passage on the last boat, sending the ledger ahead to a foreign archive while she, Elias, and Marguerite begin again where no one knows their names.
about_author: Marguerite Zhou is the pen name of a former maritime archivist who spent a decade cataloguing lighthouse logs and requisition records from forgotten coastal towns. She writes historical fiction about the people history files under 'miscellaneous.'

chapters.title: The Weight of Glass
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. A storm season opens; Coral trims the lamp, counts supplies, and adds three new names to her hidden ledger of the displaced. We learn her husband died at sea two winters past and that Marguerite, a dock orphan, now sleeps in the oil room. Emotional beat: quiet grief steadied by routine.

chapters.title: What the Tide Brings In
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. A wrecked supply skiff washes ashore carrying Elias Voss, half-drowned and carrying sealed military charts he was ordered to destroy. Coral hides him against regulation, telling herself it is only until the weather clears. Beat: first crack in her careful isolation; wary curiosity kindles.

chapters.title: Requisition Notice
chapters.summary: Coral's POV, with a brief interlude from Elias. The army posts orders: the town will be cleared in ninety days, all private papers confiscated for the official historical commission. Coral watches soldiers inventory her neighbors' lives. Beat: dread hardening into resolve — the ledger must not be surrendered.

chapters.title: Names Are Not Evidence
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Elias reveals the commission's purpose: the victors are compiling a sanitized record, and seized documents will be recopied or destroyed. He offers his knowledge of the requisition bureaucracy in exchange for silence about his desertion. Beat: uneasy alliance formed over candlelight and shared guilt.

chapters.title: The Copying Nights
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Coral, Elias, and Marguerite copy the ledger by lamplight, memorizing names in case the originals burn. Marguerite insists on writing the children's entries herself. Soldiers grow suspicious of the lighthouse's late hours. Beat: found family solidifying under pressure; tenderness threaded with fear.

chapters.title: Inspection
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Captain Reyes inspects the lighthouse and nearly finds the false wall behind the oil stores; Marguerite's quick lie about hiding contraband sugar saves them but draws a watchful eye. Coral realizes they are already suspected. Beat: terror sharpening into urgency — days, not weeks.

chapters.title: The Cartographer's Confession
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Elias admits he once drew the evacuation maps that erased villages like this one, and that his desertion was penance. Coral must decide whether forgiveness is possible. Beat: love acknowledged against duty — she chooses him knowing what he has done, not despite it.

chapters.title: Ninety Days, Spent
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. The deadline arrives early; troops move through the streets at dawn. Coral entrusts the copied ledger to a fisherman bound for a neutral port archive, keeping only the memorized names. The original is seized. Beat: sacrifice and release — the truth leaves her hands.

chapters.title: The Last Boat
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Interrogated by Reyes, Coral gives up nothing; Elias surrenders himself to buy her and Marguerite time, then escapes during the chaos of embarkation. The three reunite on the final civilian ferry as the town's lights go dark behind them. Beat: climax — everything risked, everything nearly lost.

chapters.title: Where No One Knows Our Names
chapters.summary: Coral's POV, epilogue voice. A year later, in a foreign fishing village, Coral receives word the archive has accepted the ledger and a historian has begun reading the true record aloud. She lights a small harbor beacon of her own making. Beat: resolution — memory preserved, duty transformed, family kept.
